context: The continuity repository already worked as a secondary project-memory layer, but its main JSON and latest pointer could disagree and a new session still had to read large human-oriented files before routing to the relevant evidence.
changes: Added ai-bootstrap.json as the minimal machine-first entrypoint.
Added memory/synapse-map.json as a directed context graph linking repositories, savepoints, invariants, and pending tasks.
Promoted a machine-readable JSON savepoint format for this memory-system change.
Updated ai-memory.json so machine-first bootstrap/routing is explicit and latest_savepoint is synchronized to this savepoint.
Updated latest_savepoint.record and NEXT_RUN.md to use the new bootstrap path.
impact: Future sessions can recover current XRBC state with fewer reads and less historical context.
Security-sensitive work still escalates to the canonical contract and repository evidence.
Human-readable checkpoints remain intact during the transition; no historical records are deleted.
The external memory layer improves continuity and context routing but does not change model weights or create persistent internal model state.
checks: All new machine-memory artifacts are valid JSON.
The bootstrap points to existing canonical memory, contract, latest pointer, and next-run files.
The synapse map references the current September 21 discovery and Xaman reconnect commits/pipelines.
The machine transition is marked hybrid and deletion of human-readable history remains disabled.
todo: On future savepoints, update the bootstrap current_state and synapse-map nodes/edges in the same change as ai-memory.json and latest_savepoint.record.
Add a lightweight consistency validator that fails when latest_savepoint.record, ai-memory.json, and the bootstrap disagree.
Only move additional categories to machine-primary representation after repeated session bootstraps remain contradiction-free.
